review.reason: A useful null result explaining how shared timing can create a spurious physiological association.

item.title: No evidence for modulation of the readiness potential by respiratory phase during natural breathing
item.headline: A shared timing reference can create an apparent breathing–brain link
item.authors: Lucas Jeay-Bizot, Raniyah Chishti, Uri Maoz, and Aaron Schurger
item.summary: Controlling for movement timing removed an apparent link between breathing phase and the pre-movement readiness potential. The result concerns natural breathing in the tested tasks.

evidence.question: Does breathing phase modulate the readiness potential?
evidence.method: Reanalysis of 52 participants, new recordings from 17, and simulations without direct coupling.
evidence.limitations: Task-specific findings; instructed breathing is a different condition.

explainer.finding: The apparent relationship disappeared with grouping that controlled for movement timing.
explainer.method: Researchers compared original, new, and simulated data using alternative analyses.
explainer.meaning: Two signals synchronized to the same event can appear linked to each other. Checking that shared reference can distinguish a statistical artifact from a direct physiological relationship.
explainer.limits: This does not rule out other breathing–brain relationships or settle free-will debates. The publisher currently labels the article an uncorrected proof.
